races.name: Barronstown Stud Irish European Breeders Fund (C & G) Maiden
Airlie Stud Stakes (Fillies' Group 2)

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: Trained by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Ryan Moore, this filly has strong Good-ground form including a win and a place in similar conditions, but her natural inclination is to race prominently — she has been placed at the rear of the map only because the forward positions are already filled, so her effectiveness here may be tempered by finding herself further back than suits.|

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: David Evans has fired the filly over from Britain and she won on Firm ground, but her sole Good-ground start produced a ninth; a true prominent racer by nature, she is shown in midfield here only because the forward slots are over-subscribed, and racing out of position on unfavourable going for her best form is a meaningful double concern.|

runners_data.name: Immortal Guard
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's filly has a clean record of one win and two places from two runs, both on Good ground over 6f, and she is a genuine prominent type who should slot naturally into second or third behind Ballinea Star — her course-going profile is as strong as any in the field.|

runners_data.name: Mr Predicted
runners_data.note: Completely unknown in terms of running style and lightly raced, the Joseph Patrick O'Brien booking of Dylan Browne McMonagle demands respect; the absence of form data makes her impossible to map with confidence, but she represents the main wildcard in a race that is otherwise fairly well-structured.|

runners_data.name: The Harv
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this M D O'Callaghan filly whose most recent run was a win on Soft ground, though her sole Good-ground start produced a poor effort; she is a genuine prominent type who should travel handily, but whether that Good-ground result was a fluke or a true representation is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Ballinea Star
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Donagh O'Connor's mount has won over 6f on Good ground and simply needs to replicate that performance — she sets the tempo entirely on her own terms in a small field with no pace rival to force her hand, which is as good a tactical position as a front-runner can occupy.|

races.paceDynamic: Ballinea Star is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only six fillies lining up, she should stride to the front unchallenged and dictate a measured, controlled tempo on Good ground over 6½f at the Curragh. Immortal Guard and The Harv are genuine prominent types who will sit just behind her, meaning the lead band is well populated but the fractions should remain fair rather than suicidal. Confucius and Dandyman Dan are both natural prominent/hold-up types who have been redistributed rearward on the pace map because the forward berths are already filled — they are not true closers and their effectiveness from off the pace is reduced. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently in second or third, track the controlled pace of Ballinea Star, and produce a clean turn of foot in the final furlong — the dominant profile is the handy prominent racer who is comfortable on Good ground and has the class to quicken when the tempo steadies. The field contains more pace-committed types than can realistically secure their favoured position; Immortal Guard and The Harv are best-placed to hold genuine prominent spots behind Ballinea Star, while Confucius and Dandyman Dan are likely to find themselves further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballinea Star Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ballinea Star leads at a fair gallop and the race develops into a tactical contest that rewards horses able to race prominently and quicken.
scenarios.body: If Ballinea Star leads at a fair gallop and the race develops into a tactical contest that rewards horses able to race prominently and quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and Ballinea Star steals enough of a cushion that those in her slipstream cannot close her down in 6½f.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely moderate and Ballinea Star steals enough of a cushion that those in her slipstream cannot close her down in 6½f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unexposed Talent Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Predicted — lightly raced and unknown in style — travels powerfully through the race and produces a performance beyond what the market or form book anticipates.
scenarios.body: If Mr Predicted — lightly raced and unknown in style — travels powerfully through the race and produces a performance beyond what the market or form book anticipates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace quickens faster than expected and the front rank tires, opening the door for those held up to finish through.
scenarios.body: If the early pace quickens faster than expected and the front rank tires, opening the door for those held up to finish through.

watchPoints.text: Immortal Guard is unbeaten on Good ground and races from the position she wants — watch whether W J Lee has her travelling comfortably early, as ease in running here would be a strong sign she is the main danger to the front-runner.

Mr Predicted's unknown style and the strength of the O'Brien/McMonagle combination means her early positioning in the race will be highly informative — if she travels prominently and smoothly, she could be considerably better than her sparse form suggests.

Ballinea Star's sectionals out of the stalls matter — if she is slow to begin or another filly (Immortal Guard, The Harv) pushes her wider than ideal in the first two furlongs, the controlled tempo she needs to maximise her chance could be compromised.

Dandyman Dan and Confucius are both natural prominent racers filling positions that do not reflect their preferred style — watch whether either manages to work forward early, as those who do may partially recover their natural race shape and improve their chances accordingly.

races.name: Neville Homes Summer Fillies Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Fingerpaint
runners_data.note: D K Weld's four-year-old has course form and Colin Keane in the saddle, setting up as the race's sole confirmed front-runner; her STYLE_FIT tag means she is arguably racing out of ideal role as a Prominent type asked to lead, and her recent form (1-3-7) is mixed, but uncontested lead conditions are a significant asset here.

runners_data.name: Orchidaceae
runners_data.note: Lightly raced in 2025 after a 287-day absence, W J Lee takes the ride for A Oliver; her lone win on Good ground came at this 7f trip and her last three runs on Good or similar conditions show she handles it, but the long layoff demands caution about fitness.

runners_data.name: Aviatrice
runners_data.note: David Marnane's filly arrives quickly off a 13-day turnaround after a modest return at Leopardstown; ran well in placed efforts on Good ground but her sim-going record (0 wins in 13 tries on Good) is a flag, and she is asked to repeat a prominent display without a true pace-setter's authority.

runners_data.name: Rion Rubette
runners_data.note: Michael Butler's filly has won back-to-back including a 7f Good-ground victory 15 days ago, and apprentice Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim is a practical advantage in a handicap; trainer's 2/3 recent strike rate signals live form, and her profile suits racing prominently on a genuine pace.

runners_data.name: Vega's Muse
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this Mrs John Harrington-trained four-year-old who hasn't run for 41 days after a disappointing last effort; she has two wins on Good-ish ground but was beaten out of sight last time and the step back to 7f from recent 8f runs may not be a straightforward fit.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Joseph O'Brien on this consistent hold-up mare who has finished second or third in four of her last five; she needs the pace to be honest to close from off it, and her five sim-going runs on Good have yielded two placed efforts without a win — a beneficiary of Scenario B rather than a winner of Scenario A.

runners_data.name: Nancy J
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's four-year-old returns from a lengthy 85-day absence with a hold-up style that requires a truly strong pace; her last visit to Good ground saw a placed effort at 8f, but she is untested back at 7f on this surface and the fitness query over this trip is real.

runners_data.name: Bint Majestic Roi
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's filly has won twice recently including on Good ground, but she is a genuine prominent racer pushed into a midfield role on this map because the race shape is crowded forward; her true chance is dependent on recovering that forward position early, which the STYLE_FIT discount makes less likely.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners this G M Lyons five-year-old who has course experience but whose trainer has gone 0/12 in the last 14 days; a natural prominent racer whose last two efforts on Good ground were disappointing, and the redistribution to midfield reflects a crowded prominent berth rather than her instinctive racing position.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides for M C Grassick in what is a blank 14-day record for the trainer; a front-running/prominent type that has been slotted into midfield purely because there are more forward racers than positions available — no wins on Good ground in relevant distance/going combinations and her last three runs have all been at shorter trips.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan's three-year-old arrives on a stunning six-race sequence including three consecutive wins on 7f Good ground, with Chris Hayes a key booking; the only 3yo in the field, she gets a significant weight concession and her in-form profile makes her one of the most compelling prominent-style runners in the race.

runners_data.name: She's Too Kool
runners_data.note: Rory Cleary partners Ms Claire O'Connell's three-year-old who has finished placed on Good ground but has shown hold-up tendencies and no win at 7f; 22 days between runs is unproblematic but she lacks the class record or proven form to make a compelling case from off the pace at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Fingerpaint is the only confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with a clear lead role, she should set a honest but uncontested gallop from the gates over Curragh's flat 7f. Behind her, Aviatrice, Rion Rubette, Vega's Muse, and Meriden will all press for prominent positions, creating a genuinely contested early order and ensuring the pace does not fall away. The hold-up contingent — Orchidaceae, Greydreambeliever, Nancy J, and She's Too Kool — will be furthest off a pace that should be genuine without being suicidal on Good ground. This race shape consistently favours horses racing prominently just off the leader who can travel smoothly and produce a sustained finish — closers will need the pace to be faster than it is likely to be to reel in those up close. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Bint Majestic Roi, Mallavelly, and Glory To Be are genuine prominent racers who are likely to find themselves further back than ideal, with Meriden and Rion Rubette — both in form — best placed to actually secure the positions they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fingerpaint Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Fingerpaint leads comfortably and the pace is fair but not frantic, allowing a small group to travel just off her.
scenarios.body: If Fingerpaint leads comfortably and the pace is fair but not frantic, allowing a small group to travel just off her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Spills, Closers Storm
scenarios.trigger: If the contest for prominent positions causes a faster-than-expected pace that sets up the race for the hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: If the contest for prominent positions causes a faster-than-expected pace that sets up the race for the hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Fingerpaint Unchallenged Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If rivals fail to apply any pressure and Fingerpaint is allowed to dictate an uncontested, relaxed gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: If rivals fail to apply any pressure and Fingerpaint is allowed to dictate an uncontested, relaxed gallop throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Fire
scenarios.trigger: If Bint Majestic Roi or Mallavelly manage to recover their natural prominent pitch and the race tempo suits a forward-travelling winner.
scenarios.body: If Bint Majestic Roi or Mallavelly manage to recover their natural prominent pitch and the race tempo suits a forward-travelling winner.

watchPoints.text: Meriden's hat-trick form at 7f on Good ground is the most current and relevant form in the race — if Chris Hayes secures a prominent position just off Fingerpaint, she is the single biggest danger in the field.

The cluster of prominent-style horses — Aviatrice, Rion Rubette, Vega's Muse — will contest hard for position in the first furlong, and if they press Fingerpaint faster than she wants to go, the whole race shape could invert to benefit the hold-up contingent.
Orchidaceae's 287-day absence is the sharpest fitness flag in the race; W J Lee may have to produce her fresh, and if she needs the run her 7f Good-ground form becomes academic today.

Bint Majestic Roi and Mallavelly both want to race prominently but cannot both achieve it — whichever is forced furthest back early is effectively out of the race given this flat 7f track offers limited cover for ground-making.

Nancy J's 85-day break makes her an unknown quantity returning to a 7f trip; if Ben Coen produces her late and the pace has been honest, she has the profile to hit the frame, but fitness must be assumed rather than confirmed.

races.name: Jebel Ali Racecourse And Stables Anglesey Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Beibhinn
runners_data.note: Won a 6f Good-ground maiden last time out and clearly relishes this going (2/2 on similar); Declan McDonogh partnerships with Joseph O'Brien have been in form at T14:13/63, and she will look to lead from the gate — the key question is whether Sun Goddess's pressure forces her into a race she cannot sustain.

runners_data.name: Belle Of The Ball
runners_data.note: Connections of Mrs John Harrington send her here off a 39-day break with a hood fitted; won over 5f on Soft but posted a disappointing fifth over 6f on Good, so the going and trip combination is unproven — she will need to settle better from a prominent pitch to reverse that form.

runners_data.name: Cleodolinda
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (just two runs) but both have come on Good ground, winning over 5f and chasing home over 5f at the Curragh; Donnacha Aidan O'Brien's yard is at T14:0/19 which is a cold statistic to note, though the step to 6f for a horse with a strong early position is an open question on breeding.

runners_data.name: Controlla
runners_data.note: Finished second on debut over 6f Good then ran fourteenth on the same course and surface, a wide margin swing that requires explanation; Colin Keane takes over for Robson De Aguiar, which is a notable booking upgrade, and 10 days since last run is sharp — the erratic form makes her volatile rather than dependable.

runners_data.name: Green Empress
runners_data.note: Only one run to her name — a second-place finish over 6f on Good — so she carries genuine unknown quantity; she is not a natural hold-up runner but with the front of the field likely to be congested, Dylan Browne McMonagle may find himself further back than ideal, meaning her finish will depend on whether the pace truly collapses late.

runners_data.name: Maggie Walker
runners_data.note: Won her sole start over 6f on Soft ground for David Marnane, a small trainer (T14:1/9) who pitches her straight into Group 3 company; the switch from Soft to Good is unproven and the step up in class is steep, though Luke McAteer will look to use her early speed from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Sun Goddess
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking for Aidan O'Brien (T14:8/43) is the headline draw here; she has three runs on similar Good ground all resulting in placings or wins (1W3P) and comes here just eight days after her last run, suggesting the yard is confident she is in peak form — the dual front-runner scenario is the central tactical risk to her chance.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Beaten eighth on most recent start but bounced back to win twice over 5f earlier in her form string; the step to 6f and switch to Good turf are manageable based on history, but W J Lee will need a well-run pace to capitalise from a prominent berth given her inconsistent finishing positions.

races.paceDynamic: Beibhinn and Sun Goddess are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 6f on Good turf at the Curragh, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a stolen lead. With Ryan Moore aboard Sun Goddess for Aidan O'Brien and Declan McDonogh on Beibhinn for Joseph O'Brien, neither camp will concede the front cheaply, meaning the pace is likely to be honest-to-strong from the off. Belle Of The Ball and Maggie Walker will push to track the leaders prominently, adding further compression to the early stages and ensuring the race is run at a true 6f tempo throughout. This shape — an honest, front-run gallop with a pressured early sectional — historically favours horses with a high cruising speed who can sit just off the pace and pick up powerfully in the final 2f, making prominent-to-midfield horses with proven finishing kicks the primary beneficiaries. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions; of those jostling for the front rank, Beibhinn and Sun Goddess are most likely to actually make the running, with Belle Of The Ball and Maggie Walker forced to settle slightly further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Strongest Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the Beibhinn–Sun Goddess duel sets a genuine strong gallop and the race is decided by raw talent and stamina through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the Beibhinn–Sun Goddess duel sets a genuine strong gallop and the race is decided by raw talent and stamina through the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front two burn each other out and a horse tracking in third or fourth sweeps past in the final furlong with a superior late kick.
scenarios.body: If the front two burn each other out and a horse tracking in third or fourth sweeps past in the final furlong with a superior late kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Talent Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed runners — Cleodolinda or Controlla — has significantly more ability than their limited form reveals and the honest gallop plays to their natural cruising speed.
scenarios.body: If one of the unexposed runners — Cleodolinda or Controlla — has significantly more ability than their limited form reveals and the honest gallop plays to their natural cruising speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner duel burns out sharply and horses from further back — ostensibly Green Empress — come with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If the front-runner duel burns out sharply and horses from further back — ostensibly Green Empress — come with a sustained late run.

watchPoints.text: Sun Goddess and Beibhinn will battle for the lead from gate one — watch whether either is allowed to stride clear alone or whether both are locked in a head-to-head duel, as the outcome of that contest effectively determines the race shape.

Belle Of The Ball is fitted with a hood for the first time and had a poor effort over 6f Good last time; if she fails to settle in the early stages and burns energy chasing the front-runners, her chance evaporates quickly.

Controlla's form swing — from 14th to 2nd and back again over the same course and distance — is unexplained; Colin Keane's booking adds confidence but punters should watch how she travels in the first two furlongs as a guide to whether her second-place run was the true form.

Green Empress has only one race to her name and is effectively an unknown quantity in Group 3 company; Dylan Browne McMonagle's handling of her in the early stages — whether she settles or gets involved — will be the key read on her chances.

The Curragh 6f on Good has been running true all card with multiple races over the same conditions today; sectional times from earlier races should give a strong read on whether the pace bias favours those who lead or those who come from behind.

races.name: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Fillies' And Mares' Group 1)

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Showed a smart return when fourth at Group level last time but is a naturally pace-pressing type who, in a field this saturated with prominent runners, is unlikely to get anywhere near her preferred front-rank berth — her best form at 8f on fast ground also raises a question at 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Estrange
runners_data.note: Five wins from eight runs in similar going and consistently placed at 1m2f on good ground; trainer David O'Meara in 8/63 form over the 14-day window, but Tudhope's clean positional instincts suit a race where tracking the leader closely is the key tactical requirement.

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Four placed efforts at 1m2f on good ground underline the form credentials, but Joseph O'Brien's filly is naturally drawn to racing on the pace — in a race this congested up front, she will likely find herself a position or two further back than ideal, which tempers the upside.

runners_data.name: One Look
runners_data.note: Paul Twomey's five-year-old has won or placed over 1m-1m2f on good ground and James Doyle will be sharply aware of the positional battle; the headgear flag is noted and 34 days off means she arrives fresh, but she must fight for a slot that several rivals also want.

runners_data.name: Qilin Queen
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly is the only confirmed hold-up runner in the field and her recent fourth from off the pace at 1m1f on good ground fits this scenario well; her two wins have both come at 1m2f-1m3f and she requires a genuine gallop to arrive late with any effect.

runners_data.name: Red Letter
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount has won at 9f and 10f on fast ground and is a naturally prominent type remapped toward the rear simply because of the positional log-jam — her style-fit score of 0.84 reflects how far this redistribution takes her from her optimal running position.

runners_data.name: Wemightakedlongway
runners_data.note: Visored again for Joseph O'Brien, this filly has struggled to place in recent outings and her STYLE_FIT of 0.92 flags she will be pushed back from her natural berth; form figures of 46-734 do not inspire confidence even if she secures a cleaner run.

runners_data.name: Beautify
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old steps up sharply in trip — her last five runs are all at 6f-8f — and while Ryan Moore's presence is always relevant, her recent form of 128-86 combined with an unproven stamina profile at 1m2f makes this a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Thundering On
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners the only confirmed front-runner in the race and her back-to-back wins on good and soft ground over 1m-1m2f give her genuine pace credentials; Joseph O'Brien's 13/63 trainer strike rate over 14 days is among the highest in the field and uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Listed as non-runner — no analysis applicable.

races.paceDynamic: Thundering On is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, she is set to control pace from the front on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at the Curragh. The redistribution note is significant here: Estrange, Carolina Jetstream, Nyra, Beautify, One Look, and Wemightakedlongway are all naturally prominent-running types, but this field cannot physically accommodate them all in the first two or three positions — Estrange and One Look are the most likely to genuinely secure a prominent berth given their consistent front-rank profiles at this trip, while the others will be shuffled back into roles that do not suit them. The result is a race that will be run at a controlled, honest but not scorching tempo, with one genuine pace-maker and a group of horses racing out of their natural positions immediately behind. This race shape favours genuine prominent types who can track Thundering On closely in the first two positions and quicken from a true gallop — Estrange in particular is ideally positioned given her record of winning at this trip and trip-style combination.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thundering On Controls, Estrange Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering On sets a sustainable gallop and Estrange tracks her closely throughout before asserting in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Thundering On sets a sustainable gallop and Estrange tracks her closely throughout before asserting in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering On sets a falsely slow early gallop and the race becomes a sprint finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Thundering On sets a falsely slow early gallop and the race becomes a sprint finish from 2f out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Early, Prominent Type Grabs It
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of multiple prominent types creates a scrimmage early, and one scrambles to the front and dictates on their own terms.
scenarios.body: If the redistribution of multiple prominent types creates a scrimmage early, and one scrambles to the front and dictates on their own terms.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits True Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering On is pressed or goes too hard early and the genuine hold-up runner arrives late on a genuinely testing surface.
scenarios.body: If Thundering On is pressed or goes too hard early and the genuine hold-up runner arrives late on a genuinely testing surface.

watchPoints.text: Thundering On's ability to bowl along uncontested at whatever tempo suits her makes her a structurally dangerous race-shaper: if McMonagle dictates every gear change, rivals remapped out of their natural positions will have no tactical answer.

The redistribution of five prominent-type runners — Carolina Jetstream, Nyra, Beautify, Wemightakedlongway, and Red Letter — means a scrappy early phase is possible as multiple horses contest berths there are not enough of; watch for crowding and checks between the 1m-7f marks.

Beautify's trip stamina is unproven at 1m2f given all five recorded runs are at 6f-8f; if the pace is honest she may be vulnerable in the final quarter-mile and Ryan Moore may be forced to drop her out early rather than take a hold-up position she has never tried.

Qilin Queen's chance is entirely pace-dependent — if Thundering On idles or the pace is manipulated to be slow, Qilin Queen's closing profile is effectively neutralised; monitor early fractions to gauge whether this scenario is alive.

Estrange's trainer David O'Meara is operating at 8/63 over 14 days, a modest ratio in this context — contrast with Joseph O'Brien's 13/63 across three runners — but her personal form at 1m2f on good ground is the strongest in the field and Tudhope's tactical awareness is worth monitoring at the early stages.

races.name: Reserve Ladies Derby Handicap

runners_data.name: Touch The Moon
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in this field and the race-shape pivot; T14 of 0/4 is a mild concern, and 43 days off is notable, but good-to-firm form figures (12/15) are solid and she sets the tempo regardless — her chance depends on whether that lead proves sustainable over 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Clear Quartz
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Mark Fahey carrying 147lbs, but has won over similar ground and shapes as a natural leader/prominent type who is likely to push forward and sit in second or third; form in similar going is limited (3/15) and the heavy weight is a drag over this trip.

runners_data.name: Musical Act
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare fitted with a visor, running for Ciaran Murphy who is 2/13 in the past 14 days; recent form figures of 74567 are uninspiring and she is best treated as an each-way outsider who needs a strongly-run race to produce her best.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's four-year-old arrives on the back of a win at 1m2f on good and has placed multiple times in similar conditions; prominent in style with a p headgear note, and the trainer's T14 strike of 5/34 represents a yard in decent form — one of the more interesting profiles in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Fixation
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's four-year-old has placed twice in similar going and is tactically versatile enough to sit prominently; the 35-day break is worth monitoring but the p headgear and course-compatible form figures (5/8 in similar) make her a credible participant in the sprint-finish scenario.

runners_data.name: Ob La Di
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare from JP Murtagh's yard whose recent form of 00-048 includes a couple of distant finishes and she has struggled badly in heavy ground; confirmed hold-up style suits a strongly-run race, but her best good-ground figures are well off the level needed here.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose own instincts to race forward will be thwarted by the crowded pace scenario; fitted with tp headgear and boasting two wins on equivalent ground and trip, she retains ability — but the STYLE_FIT flag and redistribution mean her chance is structurally discounted unless she does force her way through to the front.

runners_data.name: Voice Of Reason
runners_data.note: William Delahunty's six-year-old has placed three times at 1m2f+ on STA/GOO, giving her solid trip credentials; T14 of 0/1 is minimal sample but form string 122598 shows she can be competitive and her prominent profile suits tracking the lone pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan's four-year-old is 206 days off (with a jumps run 22 days ago to sharpen fitness) and wears tp headgear; a genuine hold-up type whose best form has come over longer trips on good ground — needs the pace to be genuinely testing to finish to best effect, which this race shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Great Mover
runners_data.note: WMcCreery's four-year-old has the soul of a prominent racer but is pushed back into midfield by the congestion at the front; a 0W2P record in similar going and recent placed efforts suggest ability, though the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Senna's Girl
runners_data.note: Diego Dias's four-year-old (T14: 0/0) carries tp headgear and has modest form figures in similar going (11/15); a genuine hold-up type who requires pace to be strong — form of 04305 is inconsistent and she is unlikely to be competitive unless the race is run to suit closers.

runners_data.name: Rocket Robyn
runners_data.note: Martin Hassett's four-year-old carries a fading-in-finish warning and is tagged as a hold-up type redistributed to midfield; sim-going record of 2/7 is thin and a 0W0P career profile in this type of company makes her difficult to recommend — the style flag compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: H Rogers's four-year-old is one of the crowded-out prominent types who will likely be racing further back than ideal; form of 747-83 in similar going is modest, and a 0W0P record in good-ground company means she needs things to go perfectly even if she secures her preferred position.

races.paceDynamic: Touch The Moon is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will set a controlled, unhurried tempo on good-to-firm ground over 1m2f — a trip she has won over before. Genoah, Great Mover, Cooley's Mist and Clear Quartz are all natural prominent types, but with Touch The Moon already occupying that role and the field overcrowded at the front end, most of those four will be forced to settle closer to midfield than they would prefer. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; of those redistributed, Clear Quartz and Genoah look most likely to actually push forward and achieve a position just off the pace, while Great Mover and Cooley's Mist are more likely to be squeezed back. A single, uncontested pace-setter on a flat track creating a steady gallop sets this race up classically for a horse tracking in second or third — the prominent-to-midfield profile that can sit close enough to the controlled tempo and quicken when the sprint begins will have a structural edge.

watchPoints.text: Touch The Moon sets the only pace in this race — if she is allowed to bowl along uncontested through the first half-mile, she controls the tempo entirely and makes the race for all those around her; watch her post-starting behaviour and early position.

Clear Quartz and Genoah are the two prominent types most likely to push forward and attempt to track the leader — if both succeed, the pace lifts and the race shape shifts from controlled to competitive, which would unsettle the projected odds of hold-up horses finishing fast.

Diamond Exchange is 23 days since her last run and drops in class with strong course-and-distance form — jockey Miss S A Carter (7) is a 7lb claimer, so watch the early market move to gauge whether the Harrington team are confident.

Great Mover, Cooley's Mist and Rocket Robyn are all running out of their natural positions due to field congestion — if any of these push forward aggressively from the gate, it could scramble the anticipated race shape significantly earlier than expected.

Good-to-firm ground confirmed for this race (despite the card header showing Good) — horses whose sim-going record is heavily weighted to soft or heavy conditions (Musical Act, Clear Quartz, Genoah) face an additional hidden concern that the raw form figures do not fully reflect.

races.name: Fitzpatrick's Garage Group Handicap

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with deeply unimpressive recent form — six runs without a win or place on similar going — but trainer De Aguiar has limited firepower and the 35-day break makes a return to form hard to predict; genuine deep closer who at least avoids early traffic.

runners_data.name: Bishopton
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on soft and placed twice at 6f on standard in recent starts, giving Wayne Lordan a live each-way angle if he can find a clean pitch in the prominent scramble; 13-day turnaround suggests fitness is solid, 10 of 15 runs on similar going is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Sommelier
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted and a fade-in-finish flag make Harnett's mount vulnerable late, despite a recent 6f Good win — the 5f bias in his good-going history hints the trip may just stretch him, so he needs this to be truly run.

runners_data.name: Unauthorized
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good last time and wants to race prominently, giving him every chance if he secures a clean berth without being squeezed in the opening furlong scramble; OR=86 makes him competitive but a 27-day break after a below-par effort needs explaining.

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with a fade warning and no win in five on similar going — the age and headgear (tongue-tie) suggest connections are fishing for a repeat of his earlier form, but 15th of 15 last time in this grade is hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the back of the field, but here mapped to midfield because of rear-group overcrowding; all five recent runs have been at 7f on soft or standard, making this 6f Good assignment a clear step outside his comfort zone — discount accordingly.

runners_data.name: Inishfallen
runners_data.note: Drops to a career-low OR, travels with a hood, and Colin Keane takes the ride — in-form jockey angle is the headline here, even if his true hold-up style has been pushed to midfield by field congestion; placed twice at 6f on standard, so the trip and surface are not a concern.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with a hood, and six of eight career runs on similar going with a win at the trip — Rory Mulligan's claim helps the weight, and this profile is best served if the pace is truly genuine.

runners_data.name: Nakamura
runners_data.note: Second on debut over 6f Good is a strong clue to course-and-distance suitability, and two wins and four places in nine similar-going starts speaks to consistency; wants a prominent berth but may be crowded out early in a 17-runner dash, which is the main concern.

runners_data.name: The Piper's Call
runners_data.note: Three from three on similar going with a win, two places and now steps up to handicap company — the unbeaten course-and-distance profile at the Curragh is the standout angle in the race, and Ben Coen's booking signals trainer confidence; the lack of pace pressure makes his prominent style ideal.

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: OR=74 and a visor fitted, currently in form for Adrian McGuinness who saddles three; a natural race-prominent horse who is unlikely to get that position given the field size and has been mapped to midfield — the style fit discount applies and tempers expectations even with the headgear sharpener.

runners_data.name: Midnight Dusk
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, with a 6f Good win and two places from seven similar-going starts; WJ Lee takes over from connections who have used multiple jockeys, and if he controls fractions unopposed from the front this horse is the key tactical anchor of the entire race.

runners_data.name: Real Encounter
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Harrington three-year-old who wants to race prominently and has placed at 5f Good — steps up slightly in trip here and has only one similar-going place from six starts, which is worth noting on what could be a quick surface.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has all five career runs at 5f but steps up to 6f for the first time today — the trip question is the dominant factor for McAteer's mount, and although he placed on Good ground at 5f, the extra furlong on a sound surface is unproven.

runners_data.name: Mary Shoelaces
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner or prominent racer who is very unlikely to secure that position against 16 rivals in a sprint — her two wins came over 5f, not 6f, and the step up in trip combined with the style displacement makes the apprentice rider's task considerably harder.

runners_data.name: Joyful Tidings
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type who placed at 5f Soft last time and has seven runs on similar going — needs a truly strong pace to reel in the leaders over 6f Good, and the Chris Hayes booking at least provides experienced guidance from the rear.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Power
runners_data.note: Non-runner — no analysis applicable.

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Dusk is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, crucially, faces no natural rival for the lead — she can dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front without being pressured into burning early energy. Behind her, however, the prominent berths are badly over-subscribed: Bishopton, Unauthorized, Nakamura, The Piper's Call, Real Encounter, and Fox In Flight all want to race in the first three or four lengths, creating a near-certain scramble for position between the 6f gate and the first furlong that will inevitably push several of these runners wider or further back than ideal. Clonmacash and Mary Shoelaces are genuine prominent-types who are unlikely to secure that position in this field shape and have been mapped to midfield as a consequence of the congestion. With Midnight Dusk able to control tempo and the prominent pack burning energy jostling for slots, the race shape strongly favours runners who can travel comfortably just off the pace in the first two groups — true prominent horses who find a clean passage — rather than deep hold-up types who will need a gap to open late against a field likely to finish in a compressed bunch.

watchPoints.text: Prominent logjam warning — Bishopton, Nakamura, Real Encounter, Fox In Flight and The Piper's Call all want the same early position; watch the first two furlongs for bumping, clipping heels or forced wide runs that could end chances before the race begins.

Midnight Dusk's early stride — if W J Lee gets a clean break and goes to the front unchallenged she becomes the key race-shaper; if she misses the gate or is immediately pressed by any of the prominent brigade the entire pace dynamic shifts.

Clonmacash and Mary Shoelaces are both natural prominent types who are realistically unlikely to secure that position here — if either burns energy fighting for slots they risk dropping out of contention from 2f out, watch for early signs of that struggle.

Fox In Flight is unproven at 6f having run all five previous races at 5f — if the pace is strong this trip extension could find him out in the final furlong; watch whether McAteer settles him early or pushes him into contention from the gate.

Colin Keane's booking on Inishfallen is a market intelligence signal — the horse is a hold-up type mapped toward midfield, and Keane's ability to find gaps from that position could elevate what looks on paper like a modest each-way claim into a genuine factor if the prominent pack interferes with each other.
